The FEEC theorem

One theorem collects the approximation theory of the library: static and time-dependent, semidiscrete and fully discrete, for every conforming family of every Hilbert complex.

The FEEC theorem (ConformingFamily.feec, statement ConformingFamily.Verdict). Let H be a Hilbert complex over 𝕜 = ℝ or ℂ on ℕ or ℤ (the de Rham complex HΛ(Ω), its versions with boundary conditions, an elasticity or Hessian complex, …) and let Vₕ be a conforming family of H along a filter h → 0: finite-dimensional subcomplexes with commuting cochain projections πₕ bounded in L² uniformly in h and the approximation property dist(w, Vₕ) → 0 ([AFW10], §3.3, §5.5; [AFW06]; [HS12], §3). Then:

  1. (static, static) if H has closed range and ℌʲ is finite-dimensional, the discrete Poincaré inequality holds uniformly in h, the discrete mixed Hodge Laplacian is uniformly well-posed, the harmonic gap tends to 0, πₕ eventually induces isomorphisms Hʲ(H) ≅ Hʲ(Vₕ), the mixed method is quasi-optimal and converges ([AFW10], Thms 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.8, 3.9);
  2. (wave, wave, constrained) on every window Wᵃ → ⋯ → W^{a+m-1} and for every closed constraint K, the semidiscrete Hodge wave equation ξₕ' = Lₕ ξₕ is well-posed, conserves energy, converges uniformly on bounded time intervals for every convergent family of initial values, at the rate (1 + C_P)(1 + t)² C hᵅ ‖ξ₀‖ on every rate class; K propagates iff it reduces L, the constraint residual then tends to 0, and otherwise some datum leaves K with a positive residual in the limit ([QB15], Thms 4.6, 4.7, 4.14, Prop. 4.17); these are the conclusions of the skew-adjoint and dissipative FEEC theorems for the wave operator ([HS12], Thms 3.9, 3.10 for the elliptic analogues);
  3. (heat, heat) on every window with closed range, the semidiscrete Hodge heat equation uₕ' = -Δₕ uₕ is well-posed, dissipates energy and converges for every datum, with the heat Ritz projection Rₕ = Gₕ Qₕ Δ + P_ℌₕ Qₕ built from the static mixed method ([AFW10], Thm 3.9; [Whe73]; [GHZ17]);
  4. (fully discrete, full) for every time scheme, power bounded and consistent of order p uniformly in h (the θ-schemes θ ≥ ½, implicit Euler and Crank–Nicolson are ones, DissipFEEC.thetaScheme, DissipFEEC.crankNicolson, and so is every A-stable rational scheme of order p ≥ 1 by von Neumann’s inequality, DissipFEEC.rationalScheme, among them the stability functions of A-stable implicit Runge–Kutta methods, DissipFEEC.gaussLegendre2, DissipFEEC.radauIIA2, DissipFEEC.sdirk2), the iterates of the wave and heat discretizations are stable and converge as h, τ → 0, with error at most the spatial rate plus the temporal error τᵖ ‖Lₕ^{p+1} v‖, which is O(τᵖ) uniformly in h along smooth comparisons for schemes consistent along trajectories ([BT79]; [Tho06], Ch. 7–9), and for every scheme (one-step TimeSchemes) and every datum of a rate class in D(L) the error from the comparison initial value is the spatial rate plus O(τ^{p/(p+2)}) uniformly in h (the scheme is tested on data smoothed by time averages, TimeScheme.norm_S_sub_sol_le_uniform); the explicit leapfrog scheme for the wave equation converges under the CFL condition τ ‖Lₕ‖ ≤ c < 1 ([Jol03]); the field carries forcing and inhomogeneous boundary data: the forced iterates Wₙ₊₁ = Pₕ Wₙ + gₙ have the comparison error plus the summed consistency defects (the discrete Duhamel formula, DissipFEEC.TimeScheme.Verdict.forced_iterates), and for an operator L_max ≥ L without boundary conditions and a lifting G of the boundary data the solution is G plus the mild solution with the forcing f − G' + L_max G, approximated by the lifted iterates Gₕ,ₙ + ιₕ Wₙ (lifted_iterates; the Crank–Nicolson runs of [QB15], Ch. 7, have the same structure, forced Crank–Nicolson of a compression, Feec.Instances.Lifting; their identification with a time scheme of the crown is open);
  5. (perturbed, perturbed) for every bounded dissipative B on the window (damping, Ohmic loss σ E, absorption), the Galerkin discretizations Lₕ + Pₕ B ιₕ of ξ' = (L + B) ξ and -Δₕ + Pₕ B ιₕ of u' = (-Δ + B) u (Pₕ the orthogonal projection onto Vₕ) are dissipative FEEC discretizations whose exact flow is the Dyson–Phillips perturbation, the unique semigroup generated by L + B; their Trotter–Kato cores are dense, and the dissipative and fully discrete FEEC theorems hold for every datum and every time scheme ([Paz83], §3.1, §3.3, §3.4; constrainedFEEC_perturbed, from perturbFEEC: every dissipative FEEC discretization with a dense core has consistent resolvents, which survive bounded perturbations).

With a Jackson estimate (ConformingFamily.feec_rated, statement ConformingFamily.Verdict.Rated: classes Reg s approximated in Vₕ at the order hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾ in the graph norm, [AFW10], §3.4; [Arn18], Ch. 7) all errors are O(hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾) for regular data: the mixed method (rate_static, [AFW10], Thm 3.9), the semidiscrete wave equation (rate_wave, (1 + C_P)(1 + 2t) C L hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾, [QB15], Thm 4.14), the heat equation (rate_heat, (2 + 3t) K L hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾ with K the constant of the static rate), and the fully discrete schemes (rate_full, O(hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾ + τᵖ) along smooth comparisons for schemes consistent along trajectories, and O(hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾ + τ^{p/(p+2)}) for every datum of the Jackson classes and every scheme, FullRate.wave_uniform, FullRate.heat_uniform).

Approximating families with variational crimes (ApproxComplexCrime.feec, statement ApproxComplexCrime.Verdict; [HS12], §3). For discrete differential spaces (Xₕ, 𝐝ₕ) with their own inner products and reading maps iₕ that need not be inclusions nor cochain maps, with inner-product defect ‖1 - iₕ* iₕ‖ → 0 and consistent approximation on the admissible states (the cochain defect ⟪𝐝ₕ* iₕ* y - iₕ* 𝐝* y, v⟫ enters the consistency residual): the approximating, fully discrete (every time scheme, leapfrog) and perturbed (dense core) FEEC theorems on the core, exact preservation of discrete constraints, and the Strang, residual-splitting and defect estimates of the exact-load projection; the rates are those of its rate classes. The crown consumes it on the zero-defect instance: every conforming window read as an approximating family (ConstrainedFEEC.toCrime, windowCrime, with Jₕ = 1, zero cochain defect and the discrete solutions of the window) satisfies it (crime). This identification is at the level of data; on a conforming window the field crime adds to wave, full and perturbed (stated there on the subcomplex front and its Ritz core) the Strang, residual and defect estimates. The weak-symmetry scheme (6.5) of [QB15], Ch. 6 applies ApproxComplexCrime.feec under both boundary conditions, with its rates (Feec.Instances.EinsteinBianchiFEMCrown).

The crown is assembled from the layer theorems: ConformingFamily.staticFEEC, approxFEEC and constrainedFEEC for the conforming windows (ConstrainedFEEC.toApprox with the core of the wave Ritz projection), ConstrainedFEEC.heatFEEC, and dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete with SkewFEEC.norm_S_sub_leapfrog_le and SkewFEEC.crankNicolson_signed (constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete), constrainedFEEC_perturbed, and ApproxComplexCrime.feec (from approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime, dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete and perturbFEEC); each field is the layer verdict itself. Every finite element family with bounded smoothed projections is a conforming family (Feec.Models.ConformingFamilies: Whitney forms and every admissible sequence P_rΛ, P_r⁻Λ on the cube, parallelepipeds and star-shaped domains, and the cubical Q_b⁻Λ on the cube, FEM.qMinusFamily), so the crown holds for each. It also holds for every discrete BGG complex of stacked conforming families (S Ṽₕ ⊆ Vₕ, πₕ S = S π̃ₕ): the discrete derived complexes are a conforming family of the derived complex (BGG.BoundedData.StackedFamily.derived), which has closed range under the hypotheses of the analytic BGG theorem (BGG.HilbertData.StackedFamily.bggVerdict; the Hessian, elasticity and div-div complexes, Feec.Domain.hessianFEEC, Feec.Domain.elasticityFEEC, Feec.Domain.divDivFEEC). Conforming families and their Jackson estimates transfer to every reweighted complex H.conj a (weighted inner products, variable coefficients: ConformingFamily.conj, SubcomplexFamily.Jackson.conj, for weights with uniformly bounded condition numbers), so the crown holds for them as well, e.g. for Maxwell’s equations in every linear medium given by factors ε = e† e, μ = m† m, in particular isotropic media (Feec.Instances.MaxwellMedia; anisotropic media once real factors are supplied). The physics instances read through the crown: the Einstein–Bianchi systems (4.14), (4.16) on 𝕋³, ℝ³, mirror cubes and boxes, with the TT plane waves as exact modes (Feec.Instances.EinsteinBianchiGradCurl), damped waves and Ohmic loss (Feec.Instances.Perturbed), and, for every discretization (none is constructed yet), the TSD residuals on bounded domains and Maxwell’s equations for forms (Feec.Instances.EinsteinBianchiBounded, Feec.Instances.MaxwellForms), and Maxwell’s equations in vector proxies on H¹ → H(curl) → H(div) → L² (Feec.Instances.Maxwell.vecFamily, vec_maxwellFEEC, through Feec.Domain.deRhamVec_maximalComplex_eq_map).

Sharpness and non-vacuity. Closed range of 𝔅ᵏ is necessary for the static verdict at j → k (ConformingFamily.StaticVerdict.closedRangeAt; the periodic complex has ℌ = 0, a conforming family and no static verdict). Feec.Counterexamples.Sharpness (crownSharpness) collects this with the counterexamples showing that the reducing hypothesis fails for the TSD constraint (only leaves applies to it) and the subcomplex hypothesis for non-matching polynomial pairs, and with the characterization of the bounded-projection hypothesis of the static layer: under closed range, uniformly graph-bounded cochain projections exist iff the discrete Poincaré inequality and the harmonic bound ‖q‖ ≤ c ‖P_ℌ q‖ hold uniformly (SubcomplexFamily.exists_isGraphBounded_iff, [AFW10], Thms 3.6, 3.7). Feec.Instances.CrownNonVacuity (crownNonVacuity) instantiates the rated crown on the Whitney forms of the cube: closed range with ℌ⁰ ≠ 0, a non-reducing constraint for which leaves fires, and a nonzero heat datum. Feec.Counterexamples.Sharpness (crownCorrections) also collects, by reference, the thesis corrections bearing on the crown (stacked BGG and (6.3), the second-order wave form, linearized gravity; no crown object occurs in them).

Outside the crown.

  • BGG discretizations: the BGG verdicts are in the graph norms of the domain complexes (the L² realization of the derived complex is not formalized); the regular decompositions and the finite-dimensional cohomology of the vector-valued de Rham complexes are hypotheses, no finite element family with S Ṽₕ ⊆ Vₕ is constructed (the only instances are the full families of finite-dimensional data, πₕ = id), and the weak-symmetry elements (BGG.Discrete, discrete connecting maps Πₕ S) are not stacked families: the scheme (6.5) of [QB15] enters through the crime crown, not through the BGG fields.
  • The improved L² rate is conditional on rates of the elliptic quantities η, δ, μ (ConformingFamily.rate_static_L2, [AFW10], Thm 3.11).
  • Impedance (absorbing) boundary conditions: their discretizations are dissipative FEEC discretizations with their own Ritz projections, not conforming windows, and carry no rate; with a bounded dissipative perturbation they have the perturbed verdict (ImpedanceTriple.GalerkinData.perturbed_verdict).
  • Perturbations and forcing: the perturbed verdict (perturbed) carries no rate of its own (the rate classes of L are not transferred to L + B), and forced (Duhamel) problems have no rate, semidiscrete or fully discrete (the fully discrete field bounds forced iterates against every comparison by stability; no consistency bound for a discretized load is proved).
  • No-slip Stokes and conforming elastodynamics (no conforming family of their complexes).
  • Explicit Runge–Kutta methods (polynomial stability functions, not bounded on the imaginary axis) and the sharp uniform-in-h order τᵖ along trajectories for general rational schemes (TimeScheme.IsTrajConsistent is proved for the θ-schemes only; the order τ^{p/(p+2)} holds for them as for every TimeScheme); the CFL condition of leapfrog is a hypothesis (no global inverse estimate ‖Lₕ‖ ≲ h⁻¹).
  • The sharp uniform temporal order τᵖ of rate_full holds along a smooth comparison of order p + 1 (DissipFEEC.Comparison.Smooth, supplied by DissipFEEC.Ritz.smooth from a bound of the lifted orbit); the bound of the lifted wave and heat orbits is not packaged here, and for all Jackson data the uniform order is τ^{p/(p+2)}. The nonsmooth-data estimates of parabolic smoothing (heat: self-adjoint Lₕ ≤ 0, strongly A-stable schemes, O(τᵖ/tᵖ)) are not formalized.

Main definitions

  • ConformingFamily.windowFEEC: the conforming window with a constraint; windowCrime: the same, read as an approximating family with zero defects.
  • ConstrainedFEEC.FullVerdict, ConstrainedFEEC.FullRate; ConstrainedFEEC.jacksonWaveRateClass.
  • ConformingFamily.Verdict, ConformingFamily.Verdict.Rated; ApproxComplexCrime.Verdict.

Main results

  • ConformingFamily.feec, ConformingFamily.feec_rated, ApproxComplexCrime.feec; constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete, constrainedFEEC_fullRate.

namespace Feec.HilbertComplex

The fully discrete verdict of a constrained FEEC discretization

section Full

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {c : ComplexShape ι} {W : ι → Type*}
  [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (W i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (W i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (W i)]
  [∀ i, NormedSpace ℝ (W i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower ℝ 𝕜 (W i)] {H : HilbertComplex 𝕜 c W}
  {κ : Type*}

The fully discrete verdict of a constrained FEEC discretization G: the fully discrete FEEC theorem (dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete) for every time scheme of the wave discretization (with the core of the wave Ritz projection) and of the heat discretization (with the heat core), and the error of explicit leapfrog for the wave discretization under the CFL condition, and the Hermitian signed linear systems of its Crank–Nicolson steps.

structure ConstrainedFEEC.FullVerdict (G : ConstrainedFEEC H κ) : Prop where
  /-- the fully discrete wave equation, for every time scheme -/
  wave (Θ : G.toApprox.TimeScheme) : Θ.Verdict G.toCore
  /-- the fully discrete heat equation, for every time scheme -/
  heat (hcr : ∀ i, H.ClosedRangeAt i) (hb : ∀ i, G.IsGraphBounded i)
    (Θ : G.toHeat.TimeScheme) : Θ.Verdict (G.heatCore hcr hb)
  /-- explicit leapfrog for the wave equation under the CFL condition `τ ‖Lₕ‖ ≤ c < 1`: the
  semidiscrete rate plus the error of the first step and a second-order temporal error -/
  leapfrog {T : ℝ} (R : G.toApprox.RateClass T) {x : PiLp 2 W} (hx : x ∈ R.Data) (h : κ)
    (v : G.toApprox.X h) {τ c : ℝ} (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) (hc : τ * ‖G.toApprox.L h‖ ≤ c) (hc1 : c < 1)
    {w : ℕ → G.toApprox.X h} (hw : TimeStepping.IsLeapfrog (G.toApprox.L h) τ w) (h0 : w 0 = v)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : (n : ℝ) * τ ∈ Icc 0 T) :
    ‖G.toApprox.S (n * τ) x - G.toApprox.incl h (w n)‖ ≤
      (R.C + ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * R.C' * (n * τ)) * (R.meshSize h ^ R.α * R.classNorm x) +
        ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * ‖R.p x h 0 - v‖ +
        ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * (√(1 + c) * ‖w 1 - exp ((τ : 𝕜) • G.toApprox.L h) v‖ / √(1 - c) +
          n * τ * τ ^ 2 * ‖(G.toApprox.L h ^ 3) v‖ / (3 * (1 - c)))
  /-- the linear systems of Crank–Nicolson for the wave equation: in a basis `b` of `Xₕ` with
  signs `ε i = ±1` adapted to it (basis functions of different signs orthogonal, `Lₕ` coupling
  only opposite signs), the signed matrix `diag(ε) (M + (τₕ/2) K)` (Gram matrix `M`, stiffness `K`
  of `Lₕ`) is Hermitian and has the coefficients of the iterate `Pₕ v` as the unique solution of
  its system, so MINRES applies (bases indexed by `Fin m`, to which every finite basis
  reindexes) -/
  crankNicolson_signed {τ : κ → ℝ} (hτ : ∀ h, 0 < τ h) (h : κ) {m : ℕ}
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin m) 𝕜 (G.toApprox.X h)) (ε : Fin m → ℝ)
    (hε : ∀ i, ε i * ε i = 1) (hMε : ∀ i j, ⟪b i, b j⟫_𝕜 ≠ 0 → ε i = ε j)
    (hKε : ∀ i j, ⟪b i, G.toApprox.L h (b j)⟫_𝕜 ≠ 0 → ε i = -ε j) (v : G.toApprox.X h) :
    (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (ε i : 𝕜)) * (Matrix.gram 𝕜 b +
        ((τ h / 2 : ℝ) : 𝕜) • TimeStepping.stiffness b (G.toApprox.L h))).IsHermitian ∧
      ∀ w, (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (ε i : 𝕜)) * (Matrix.gram 𝕜 b +
          ((τ h / 2 : ℝ) : 𝕜) • TimeStepping.stiffness b (G.toApprox.L h))).mulVec w =
        (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (ε i : 𝕜)) * (Matrix.gram 𝕜 b -
          ((τ h / 2 : ℝ) : 𝕜) • TimeStepping.stiffness b (G.toApprox.L h))).mulVec
            (b.equivFun v) ↔
      w = b.equivFun ((G.toApprox.crankNicolson τ hτ).P h v)

The fully discrete FEEC theorem for a constrained FEEC discretization: wave and heat, every time scheme, leapfrog under the CFL condition, and the Hermitian signed systems of Crank–Nicolson.

theorem constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete (G : ConstrainedFEEC H κ) : G.FullVerdict :=
  ⟨fun Θ => dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete G.toCore Θ,
    fun hcr hb Θ => dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete (G.heatCore hcr hb) Θ,
    G.toApprox.norm_S_sub_leapfrog_le,
    fun hτ h _ b ε hε hMε hKε v => G.toApprox.crankNicolson_signed hτ h b ε hε hMε hKε v⟩

variable {ρ : Type*}

The wave rate class of a Jackson estimate: the rate class of the wave Ritz projection (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.toApprox) on the data of ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson.

abbrev ConstrainedFEEC.jacksonWaveRateClass (G : ConstrainedFEEC H κ) (J : G.Jackson ρ) (T : ℝ)
    (s : ρ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) : G.toApprox.RateClass T :=
  (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson G J T s hL).toApprox

The fully discrete rates of a Jackson estimate J of a constrained FEEC discretization G: for every time scheme consistent of order p along trajectories and every smooth comparison of order p + 1 of the wave rate class (jacksonWaveRateClass) or of the heat rate class (ConstrainedFEEC.jacksonHeatRateClass of the total Jackson estimate), the fully discrete error is the spatial rate plus O(τₕᵖ), uniformly in h; for every time scheme and every datum of these classes, it is the spatial rate plus O(τₕ^{p/(p+2)}), uniformly in h.

structure ConstrainedFEEC.FullRate (G : ConstrainedFEEC H κ) (J : G.Jackson ρ) : Prop where
  /-- the fully discrete wave equation -/
  wave {T : ℝ} (s : ρ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (Θ : G.toApprox.TimeScheme) {K : ℝ}
    (hΘ : Θ.IsTrajConsistent K)
    (Sm : (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).toComparison.Smooth (Θ.p + 1)) {x : PiLp 2 W}
    (hx : x ∈ (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).Data) (hxs : x ∈ Sm.Data) (h : κ)
    (v : G.toApprox.X h) {n : ℕ} (hn : (n : ℝ) * Θ.τ h ∈ Icc 0 T) :
    ‖G.toApprox.S (n * Θ.τ h) x - Θ.sol h v n‖ ≤
      (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C * (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).meshSize h ^
          (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).α * (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).classNorm x +
        ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * Θ.M T * (‖(G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).p x h 0 - v‖ +
          n * Θ.τ h * (K * Θ.τ h ^ Θ.p * Sm.B x + (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C' *
            (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).meshSize h ^ (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).α *
              (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).classNorm x))
  /-- the fully discrete heat equation -/
  heat (hcr : ∀ i, H.ClosedRangeAt i) (hb : ∀ i, G.IsGraphBounded i) {T : ℝ} (s : ρ)
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (Θ : G.toHeat.TimeScheme) {K : ℝ} (hΘ : Θ.IsTrajConsistent K)
    (Sm : (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).toComparison.Smooth (Θ.p + 1))
    {x : PiLp 2 W} (hx : x ∈ (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).Data)
    (hxs : x ∈ Sm.Data) (h : κ) (v : G.toHeat.X h) {n : ℕ} (hn : (n : ℝ) * Θ.τ h ∈ Icc 0 T) :
    ‖G.toHeat.S (n * Θ.τ h) x - Θ.sol h v n‖ ≤
      (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C *
          (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).meshSize h ^
            (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).α *
          (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).classNorm x +
        ‖G.toHeat.incl h‖ * Θ.M T *
          (‖(G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).p x h 0 - v‖ +
            n * Θ.τ h * (K * Θ.τ h ^ Θ.p * Sm.B x +
              (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C' *
                (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).meshSize h ^
                  (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).α *
                (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).classNorm x))
  /-- the fully discrete wave equation for every datum of the Jackson class and every time
  scheme: the spatial rate plus `O(τₕ^{p/(p+2)})`, uniformly in `h` -/
  wave_uniform {T : ℝ} (s : ρ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (Θ : G.toApprox.TimeScheme) {x : PiLp 2 W}
    (hx : x ∈ (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).Data) (h : κ) (v : G.toApprox.X h) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : (n : ℝ) * Θ.τ h ∈ Icc 0 T) (hτT : Θ.τ h ^ ((Θ.p : ℝ) / (Θ.p + 2)) ≤ T) :
    ‖G.toApprox.S (n * Θ.τ h) x - Θ.sol h v n‖ ≤
      ((G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C +
          ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C' * (n * Θ.τ h)) *
          ((G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).meshSize h ^ (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).α *
            (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).classNorm x) +
        ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * (Θ.M T * ‖(G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).p x h 0 - v‖ +
          (1 + Θ.M T) * (Θ.p + 1) * G.toApprox.boundConst *
            (2 * (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C +
              ‖G.toApprox.incl h‖ * (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).C' * T) *
            ((G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).meshSize h ^ (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).α *
              (G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).classNorm x) +
          Θ.τ h ^ ((Θ.p : ℝ) / (Θ.p + 2)) * ((1 + Θ.M T) * (Θ.p + 1) * G.toApprox.boundConst *
            ‖DissipFEEC.genExt H.wave x‖ + Θ.M T * Θ.K * (n * Θ.τ h) * 2 ^ (Θ.p + 1) *
              ‖(G.jacksonWaveRateClass J T s hL).p x h 0‖))
  /-- the fully discrete heat equation for every datum of the Jackson class and every time
  scheme: the spatial rate plus `O(τₕ^{p/(p+2)})`, uniformly in `h` -/
  heat_uniform (hcr : ∀ i, H.ClosedRangeAt i) (hb : ∀ i, G.IsGraphBounded i) {T : ℝ}
    (s : ρ) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (Θ : G.toHeat.TimeScheme) {x : PiLp 2 W}
    (hx : x ∈ (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).Data) (h : κ)
    (v : G.toHeat.X h) {n : ℕ} (hn : (n : ℝ) * Θ.τ h ∈ Icc 0 T)
    (hτT : Θ.τ h ^ ((Θ.p : ℝ) / (Θ.p + 2)) ≤ T) :
    ‖G.toHeat.S (n * Θ.τ h) x - Θ.sol h v n‖ ≤
      ((G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C + ‖G.toHeat.incl h‖ *
          (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C' * (n * Θ.τ h)) *
          ((G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).meshSize h ^
              (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).α *
            (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).classNorm x) +
        ‖G.toHeat.incl h‖ * (Θ.M T *
            ‖(G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).p x h 0 - v‖ +
          (1 + Θ.M T) * (Θ.p + 1) * G.toHeat.boundConst *
            (2 * (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C + ‖G.toHeat.incl h‖ *
              (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).C' * T) *
            ((G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).meshSize h ^
                (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).α *
              (G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).classNorm x) +
          Θ.τ h ^ ((Θ.p : ℝ) / (Θ.p + 2)) * ((1 + Θ.M T) * (Θ.p + 1) * G.toHeat.boundConst *
            ‖DissipFEEC.genExt (-H.hodgeLaplacian) x‖ + Θ.M T * Θ.K * (n * Θ.τ h) *
              2 ^ (Θ.p + 1) * ‖(G.jacksonHeatRateClass hcr hb (G.totalJackson J) s hL T).p x h 0‖))

The fully discrete rates of a Jackson estimate (ConstrainedFEEC.FullRate), the field rate_smooth_iterates of the fully discrete verdicts at the Jackson rate classes.

theorem constrainedFEEC_fullRate (G : ConstrainedFEEC H κ) (J : G.Jackson ρ) : G.FullRate J :=
  ⟨fun _ _ _ Θ _ hΘ Sm _ hx hxs h v _ hn =>
      ((constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete G).wave Θ).rate_smooth_iterates hΘ _ Sm hx hxs h v hn,
    fun hcr hb _ _ _ _ Θ _ hΘ Sm _ hx hxs h v _ hn =>
      ((constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete G).heat hcr hb Θ).rate_smooth_iterates hΘ _ Sm hx hxs h v hn,
    fun s _ hL Θ _ hx h v _ hn hτT => ((constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete G).wave Θ).rate_uniform_iterates
      _ hx ((ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson G J _ s hL).mem_domain _ hx) h v hn hτT,
    fun hcr hb _ _ _ _ Θ _ hx h v _ hn hτT =>
      ((constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete G).heat hcr hb Θ).rate_uniform_iterates _ hx hx.1.1 h v hn hτT⟩

end Full

The crown for approximating families with variational crimes

section Crime

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {c : ComplexShape ι} {W : ι → Type*}
  [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (W i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (W i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (W i)]
  [∀ i, NormedSpace ℝ (W i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower ℝ 𝕜 (W i)] {H : HilbertComplex 𝕜 c W}
  {κ : Type*}

namespace ApproxComplexCrime

open ApproxFEEC

The conclusions of the FEEC theorem for approximating families (ApproxComplexCrime.feec) of discrete differential spaces (Xₕ, 𝐝ₕ) with reading maps iₕ that need not be cochain maps nor isometric ([HS12], §3): the approximating, fully discrete and perturbed FEEC theorems of the crime front ofComplexCrime F on its core, the discrete generator, the discrete constraints, and the complex-level estimates of the exact-load projection Rₕ y = (1 - Lₕ)⁻¹ iₕ* (1 - L) y (Strang lemma, residual splitting into the inner-product defect, the graph-norm approximation error and the cochain defect, defect bound, and their limits). The rates are the fields wave.rate and (full Θ).rate_* at the rate classes of ofComplexCrime F (e.g. rateClass_of_split, galerkinRateClass).

structure Verdict (F : ApproxComplexCrime H κ) : Prop where
  /-- the approximating FEEC theorem of the crime front on its core -/
  wave : (ofComplexCrime F).Verdict (ofComplexCrimeCore F)
  /-- the fully discrete FEEC theorem, for every time scheme -/
  full (Θ : (ofComplexCrime F).TimeScheme) : Θ.Verdict (ofComplexCrimeCore F)
  /-- explicit leapfrog under the CFL condition `τ ‖Lₕ‖ ≤ c < 1` -/
  leapfrog {T : ℝ} (R : (ofComplexCrime F).RateClass T) {x : PiLp 2 W} (hx : x ∈ R.Data) (h : κ)
    (v : (ofComplexCrime F).X h) {τ c : ℝ} (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) (hc : τ * ‖(ofComplexCrime F).L h‖ ≤ c)
    (hc1 : c < 1) {w : ℕ → (ofComplexCrime F).X h}
    (hw : TimeStepping.IsLeapfrog ((ofComplexCrime F).L h) τ w) (h0 : w 0 = v) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : (n : ℝ) * τ ∈ Icc 0 T) :
    ‖(ofComplexCrime F).S (n * τ) x - (ofComplexCrime F).incl h (w n)‖ ≤
      (R.C + ‖(ofComplexCrime F).incl h‖ * R.C' * (n * τ)) *
          (R.meshSize h ^ R.α * R.classNorm x) +
        ‖(ofComplexCrime F).incl h‖ * ‖R.p x h 0 - v‖ +
        ‖(ofComplexCrime F).incl h‖ *
          (√(1 + c) * ‖w 1 - exp ((τ : 𝕜) • (ofComplexCrime F).L h) v‖ / √(1 - c) +
            n * τ * τ ^ 2 * ‖((ofComplexCrime F).L h ^ 3) v‖ / (3 * (1 - c)))
  /-- the perturbed FEEC theorem for every bounded perturbation, when the core is dense -/
  perturbed (hZ : (ofComplexCrimeCore F).Data.topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (P : (ofComplexCrime F).Perturbation) : P.Verdict (P.core (ofComplexCrimeCore F) hZ)
  /-- an `Lₕ`-invariant subspace of `Xₕ` is preserved exactly by the discrete solutions -/
  invariant (h : κ) (Kh : Submodule 𝕜 (F.toFamily.X h)) (hKh : ∀ v ∈ Kh, F.toFamily.L h v ∈ Kh)
    {v : F.toFamily.X h} (hv : v ∈ Kh) (t : ℝ) : ((ofComplexCrime F).group h).S t v ∈ Kh
  /-- and if it is read inside `K`, the residual of its discrete solutions is `0` -/
  residual_eq_zero (h : κ) (Kh : Submodule 𝕜 (F.toFamily.X h))
    (hKh : ∀ v ∈ Kh, F.toFamily.L h v ∈ Kh)
    (hKK : Kh.map (F.toFamily.incl h : F.toFamily.X h →ₗ[𝕜] PiLp 2 W) ≤ F.K)
    {v : F.toFamily.X h} (hv : v ∈ Kh) (t : ℝ) :
    infDist ((ofComplexCrime F).sol h v t) (F.K : Set (PiLp 2 W)) = 0
  /-- the Strang lemma: best approximation plus residual -/
  strang (h : κ) (y z : PiLp 2 W) (w : F.toFamily.X h) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (hres : ∀ v, ‖⟪w - F.toFamily.L h w, v⟫_𝕜 - ⟪z, F.toFamily.incl h v⟫_𝕜‖ ≤
      ε * (‖v‖ + ‖F.toFamily.D h v‖)) :
    ‖y - F.toFamily.incl h (F.toFamily.load h z)‖ ≤
      ‖y - F.toFamily.incl h w‖ + 8 * F.toFamily.boundConst * ε
  /-- the residual splits into the inner-product defect, the graph-norm approximation error and
  the cochain defect -/
  residual_le (h : κ) (y : H.wave.domain) (w : F.toFamily.X h) {δ : ℝ}
    (hδ : ∀ v, ‖⟪F.toFamily.cochainDefect h y, v⟫_𝕜‖ ≤ δ * (‖v‖ + ‖F.toFamily.D h v‖))
    (v : F.toFamily.X h) :
    ‖⟪w - F.toFamily.L h w, v⟫_𝕜 - ⟪(y : PiLp 2 W) - H.wave y, F.toFamily.incl h v⟫_𝕜‖ ≤
      (‖1 - F.toFamily.J h‖ * (‖w‖ + ‖F.toFamily.D h w‖) +
        F.toFamily.boundConst * (‖(y : PiLp 2 W) - F.toFamily.incl h w‖ +
          ‖H.totalD ⟨y, y.2.1⟩ - F.toFamily.incl h (F.toFamily.D h w)‖) + δ) *
        (‖v‖ + ‖F.toFamily.D h v‖)
  /-- the defect bound `‖Rₕ z - iₕ* y‖ ≤ ‖1 - Jₕ‖ ‖Rₕ z‖ + C ‖y - iₕ Rₕ z‖` -/
  defect_le (h : κ) (y z : PiLp 2 W) :
    ‖F.toFamily.load h z - (F.toFamily.incl h).adjoint y‖ ≤
      ‖1 - F.toFamily.J h‖ * ‖F.toFamily.load h z‖ +
        F.toFamily.boundConst * ‖y - F.toFamily.incl h (F.toFamily.load h z)‖
  /-- the exact-load projection converges at every admissible state -/
  tendsto_reading {y : PiLp 2 W} (hy : y ∈ F.A) :
    Tendsto (fun h => ‖y - F.toFamily.incl h (F.toFamily.load h (y - waveExt H y))‖) F.l (𝓝 0)
  /-- and its defect tends to `0` there -/
  tendsto_defect {y : PiLp 2 W} (hy : y ∈ F.A) :
    Tendsto (fun h => ‖F.toFamily.load h (y - waveExt H y) - (F.toFamily.incl h).adjoint y‖) F.l
      (𝓝 0)
  /-- the discrete generator is `Lₕ = 𝐝ₕ - 𝐝ₕ*` -/
  generator (h : κ) : (ofComplexCrime F).L h = F.toFamily.D h - (F.toFamily.D h).adjoint

The FEEC theorem for approximating families with variational crimes. For every approximating family F of discrete differential spaces of a Hilbert complex (ApproxComplexCrime: inner-product defect ‖1 - iₕ* iₕ‖ → 0 and consistent approximation on the admissible states, the reading maps need not be cochain maps): the approximating FEEC theorem on the core, the discrete generator 𝐝ₕ - 𝐝ₕ*, the fully discrete theorems for every time scheme and for leapfrog under the CFL condition, the perturbed theorems for every bounded perturbation (dense core), exact preservation of discrete constraints, and the Strang, residual and defect estimates with their limits. The conforming windows give the zero-defect instance (ConstrainedFEEC.toCrime, ConformingFamily.Verdict.crime); scheme (6.5) is an instance (Feec.Instances.EinsteinBianchiFEMCrown). [HS12], §3; [BT79]; [Paz83], §3.4

theorem feec (F : ApproxComplexCrime H κ) : F.Verdict :=
  ⟨(approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).1, fun Θ => dissipFEEC_fullyDiscrete _ Θ,
    fun R _ hx h v _ _ hτ hc hc1 _ hw h0 _ hn =>
      (ofComplexCrime F).norm_S_sub_leapfrog_le R hx h v hτ hc hc1 hw h0 hn,
    fun hZ P => perturbFEEC _ hZ P,
    fun h Kh hKh _ hv t => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.1 h Kh hKh _ hv t,
    fun h Kh hKh hKK _ hv t => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.1 h Kh hKh hKK _ hv t,
    fun h y z w _ hε hres => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.2.1 h y z w _ hε hres,
    fun h y w _ hδ v => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.2.2.1 h y w _ hδ v,
    (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.2.2.2.1,
    fun hy => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 _ hy,
    fun hy => (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2 _ hy,
    (approxFEEC_ofComplexCrime F).2.1⟩

end ApproxComplexCrime

end Crime

The crown

section Crown

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoidWithOne α] [IsCancelAdd α] [CharZero α]
  {V : α → Type*} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (V i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (V i)]
  [∀ i, CompleteSpace (V i)] [∀ i, NormedSpace ℝ (V i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower ℝ 𝕜 (V i)]
  {H : HilbertComplex 𝕜 (ComplexShape.up α) V} {κ : Type*}

namespace ConformingFamily

The conforming window with a constraint: the window Vₕᵃ → ⋯ → Vₕ^{a+m-1} of F (ConformingFamily.window) with the closed constraint K, a constrained FEEC discretization of the window H.window a m.

abbrev windowFEEC (F : ConformingFamily H κ) (a : α) (m : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    ConstrainedFEEC (H.window a m) κ :=
  (F.window a m).withConstraint K hK

omit [∀ i, NormedSpace ℝ (V i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower ℝ 𝕜 (V i)] in

The projections of the conforming window are bounded in the graph norm in every degree.

theorem isGraphBounded_windowFEEC (F : ConformingFamily H κ) (a : α) (m : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    ∀ i, (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).IsGraphBounded i :=
  (F.window a m).isGraphBounded_toSubcomplexFamily

The conforming window as an approximating family with variational crimes: the window with the constraint K (windowFEEC) read as an approximating family of discrete differential spaces with zero inner-product and cochain defects (ConstrainedFEEC.toCrime).

abbrev windowCrime (F : ConformingFamily H κ) (a : α) (m : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    ApproxComplexCrime (H.window a m) κ :=
  (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toCrime

The conclusions of the FEEC theorem (feec) for a conforming family F: the static FEEC theorem in every degree, and on every window with every closed constraint the semidiscrete wave and heat FEEC theorems, the fully discrete ones, and the perturbed ones for every bounded dissipative B.

structure Verdict (F : ConformingFamily H κ) : Prop where
  /-- the static FEEC theorem in every degree with finite-dimensional harmonic forms
  ([AFW2010], Thms 3.4–3.9) -/
  static (hcr : ∀ i, H.ClosedRangeAt i) (j : α) [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (H.harmonic j)] :
    F.StaticVerdict j
  /-- the approximating FEEC theorem for the wave equation on every window with every closed
  constraint, hence the skew-adjoint and dissipative ones -/
  wave (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toApprox.Verdict (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toCore
  /-- the constrained FEEC theorem on every window with every closed constraint
  ([QuennevilleBelair2015], Thms 4.6, 4.7, 4.14, Prop. 4.17) -/
  constrained (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).Verdict
  /-- the heat FEEC theorem on every window with closed range, with every closed constraint -/
  heat (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i))))
    (hcr : ∀ i, (H.window a m).ClosedRangeAt i) :
    (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toHeat.Verdict
      ((F.windowFEEC a m K hK).heatCore hcr (F.isGraphBounded_windowFEEC a m K hK))
  /-- the fully discrete wave and heat FEEC theorems on every window with every closed
  constraint, for every time scheme, and leapfrog under the CFL condition -/
  full (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).FullVerdict
  /-- the perturbed FEEC theorems on every window with every closed constraint and every bounded
  dissipative `B`: the damped wave and perturbed heat equations ([Pazy1983], §3.1, §3.3, §3.4) -/
  perturbed (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i))))
    (B : (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)) →L[𝕜] PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i))
    (hB : ∀ x, RCLike.re ⟪B x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ 0) : (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).PerturbedVerdict B hB
  /-- the zero-defect instance of the FEEC theorem for approximating families
  (`ApproxComplexCrime.feec`): every window with every closed constraint, read as an approximating
  family with zero defects (`windowCrime`; [HolstStern2012], §3) -/
  crime (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    (F.windowCrime a m K hK).Verdict

The FEEC theorem. For every conforming family F of a Hilbert complex on ℕ or ℤ: the static FEEC theorem in every degree (closed range, finite-dimensional harmonic forms), and on every window with every closed constraint the semidiscrete wave FEEC theorem (approximating and constrained), the heat FEEC theorem (closed range of the window), the fully discrete theorems for every time scheme and for leapfrog under the CFL condition, and the perturbed theorems for every bounded dissipative perturbation. [AFW10], Thms 3.4–3.9; [QB15], Thms 4.6, 4.7, 4.14, Prop. 4.17; [BT79]; [Paz83], §3.1, §3.3, §3.4

theorem feec (F : ConformingFamily H κ) : F.Verdict :=
  ⟨fun hcr j _ => F.staticFEEC hcr j,
    fun a m K hK => approxFEEC _ (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toCore,
    fun a m K hK => constrainedFEEC (F.windowFEEC a m K hK),
    fun a m K hK hcr => (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).heatFEEC hcr (F.isGraphBounded_windowFEEC a m K hK),
    fun a m K hK => constrainedFEEC_fullyDiscrete (F.windowFEEC a m K hK),
    fun a m K hK B hB => constrainedFEEC_perturbed (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) B hB,
    fun a m K hK => (F.windowCrime a m K hK).feec⟩

variable {ρ : Type*}

The rated conclusions of the FEEC theorem (feec_rated) for a conforming family F with a Jackson estimate J: those of the FEEC theorem, and the rates hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾ of the mixed method, of the semidiscrete wave and heat equations and of the fully discrete schemes for s-regular data.

structure Verdict.Rated (F : ConformingFamily H κ) (J : F.Jackson ρ) : Prop
    extends F.Verdict where
  /-- the rate of the mixed method, with closed range in the degrees of the problem
  ([AFW2010], Thm 3.9) -/
  rate_static (s : ρ) {i j k : α} (hij : (ComplexShape.up α).Rel i j)
    (hjk : (ComplexShape.up α).Rel j k) (hj : H.ClosedRangeAt j) (hk : H.ClosedRangeAt k) :
    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ {f : V j} {σ : H.domainSpace i} {u : H.domainSpace j} {p : H.harmonic j},
    H.IsMixedSolution i j k f σ u p → ∀ {L : ℝ}, 0 ≤ L →
    J.Reg s i L (H.domainIncl i σ) → J.Reg s j L (H.domainIncl j u) →
    J.Reg s j L (H.domainIncl j (H.boundaryPart j (H.domainIncl j u))) →
    J.Reg s j L (p : V j) → ∀ h : κ,
    (F.V h).mixedError hij hjk f σ u p ≤ K * L * J.meshSize h ^ J.ord s
  /-- the rate `(1 + C_P)(1 + 2t) C L hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾` of the semidiscrete wave equation on every window
  ([QuennevilleBelair2015], Thm 4.14) -/
  rate_wave (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) {T : ℝ} (s : ρ) {L : ℝ}
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) {x : PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)}
    (hx : x ∈ (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s
      hL).Data) (h : κ) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc 0 T) :
    ‖(H.window a m).waveGroup.S t x - (H.window a m).totalD.graphFst
        ((F.windowFEEC a m K hK).discrete h (waveLift (H.window a m)
          ⟨x, (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s
            hL).mem_domain x hx⟩) t)‖ ≤
      (1 + ellipticConst (H.window a m)) * (1 + 2 * t) *
        ((ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s hL).C *
          (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s
            hL).meshSize h ^
            (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s hL).α *
          (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m) T s
            hL).classNorm x)
  /-- the rate `(2 + 3t) K L hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾` of the semidiscrete heat equation on every window, `K` the
  constant of the static rate ([AFW2010], Thm 3.9 along the heat flow) -/
  rate_heat (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i))))
    (hcr : ∀ i, (H.window a m).ClosedRangeAt i) (s : ρ) :
    ∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ {L : ℝ}, 0 ≤ L →
    ∀ {T : ℝ} {x : PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)},
      x ∈ (-(H.window a m).hodgeLaplacian).sqDomain →
      (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toHeat.S t x ∈
        (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).heatReg hcr ((F.windowFEEC a m K hK).totalJackson (J.window a m))
          s L) → ∀ (h : κ), ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T,
    ‖(F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toHeat.S t x - (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).toHeat.sol h
        ((F.windowFEEC a m K hK).ritzR h (x, DissipFEEC.genExt (-(H.window a m).hodgeLaplacian) x))
          t‖ ≤
      (2 + 3 * t) * C * L * J.meshSize h ^ J.ord s
  /-- the fully discrete rates on every window: the spatial rate plus `O(τᵖ)` along smooth
  comparisons, and plus `O(τ^{p/(p+2)})` for every Jackson datum -/
  rate_full (a : α) (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule 𝕜 (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set (PiLp 2 fun i : Fin m => V (a + i)))) :
    (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).FullRate (J.window a m)

The FEEC theorem with rates. For every conforming family F of a Hilbert complex on ℕ or ℤ with a Jackson estimate J: the FEEC theorem (feec), and for s-regular data with bound L the errors of the mixed method, of the semidiscrete wave and heat equations on every window and of the fully discrete schemes are O(L hᵒʳᵈ⁽ˢ⁾), plus O(τᵖ) for the fully discrete ones along smooth comparisons and O(τ^{p/(p+2)}) for every datum. [AFW10], Thm 3.9; [QB15], Thm 4.14; [BT79]

theorem feec_rated (F : ConformingFamily H κ) (J : F.Jackson ρ) : Verdict.Rated F J :=
  ⟨F.feec, fun s _ _ _ hij hjk hj hk => F.rate J s hij hjk hj hk,
    fun a m K hK _ s _ hL _ hx h _ ht => (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).rate_le
      (ConstrainedFEEC.RateClass.ofJackson _ (J.window a m) _ s hL) hx h ht,
    fun a m K hK hcr s => (F.windowFEEC a m K hK).rate_heat hcr
      (F.isGraphBounded_windowFEEC a m K hK) _ s,
    fun a m K hK => constrainedFEEC_fullRate (F.windowFEEC a m K hK) (J.window a m)⟩

end ConformingFamily

end Crown

end Feec.HilbertComplex
